request.prompt:
You are clustering code review findings from the same PR. For each PAIR below, decide whether the two findings describe the SAME underlying issue — same root cause in the same code location. Different wording is fine. A finding about a DIFFERENT defect in the same file or function is NOT the same issue. Severity or aspect differences of the same root cause ARE the same issue.


For THIS scoring pass, duplicate equivalence is stricter than sharing a root cause.
You must compare the COMPLETE MATERIAL CLAIMS, including mechanism, triggering
conditions, execution path, and consequence. The same line or broad concern does
not establish equivalence. A report of wrong-category selection, a case/rename
mismatch, a crash, and a silent fallback are different claims even at one lookup.
An inactive/unbound API concern and an alleged active user-facing failure differ.
A compound report with an additional material claim does NOT equal its subset.
Differences only in wording, severity, or hedging do not create separate claims.
If the claimed mechanisms, triggers or consequences conflict, or one report adds
an unsupported/different material factual claim, return same=false. You are NOT
verifying which claim is true; do not repair or reinterpret either report to make
them match. If unsure whether their full claims are equivalent, return false.

For every numbered pair, extract what A and B actually CLAIM into mechanism,
trigger and consequence. Then list material_differences and give your equivalence
verdict, confidence and reason. same=true requires no material differences.
Return ONLY this JSON object, with EVERY pair index exactly once:

PAIR 14:
A: In sharing mode parseRefreshTokenResponse returns data reduced to {access_token, refresh_token: "refresh_token"} (the broken minimum schema strips the rest and injects the placeholder), and this spread overwrites o365AuthCredentials' real refresh token before the credential update persists it. The stored Office365 credential's refresh_token becomes the literal string "refresh_token" and its expiry timestamp is never updated (stale expiry forces a sync call on every operation); if credential sharing is later disabled or the endpoint removed, the credential can never refresh again and the user must re-authenticate.
B: minimumTokenResponseSchema uses [z.string().toString()] which evaluates to literal key '[object Object]', causing Zod to strip fields and a fake refresh_token to be persisted, destroying stored credentials

A: packages/app-store/office365video/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:93 — Entire response body is written over the credential key, dropping refresh_token when the sync endpoint returns only an access token, permanently breaking refresh
B: packages/app-store/office365video/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:93 — Raw refresh response is persisted as the credential key without parseRefreshTokenResponse (unlike office365calendar), so the minimal sync response silently drops refresh_token from the stored credential.

PAIR 16:
A: The connection setup now performs an unconditional token refresh - a fetch to login.salesforce.com plus a prisma credential write - on every SalesforceCalendarService instantiation, where the previous code created the jsforce Connection lazily and refreshed only when an API call actually needed a new token. Every booking operation touching a Salesforce calendar now incurs a synchronous round-trip to Salesforce and a DB write, burns Salesforce token-endpoint rate limits, and fails outright whenever Salesforce's token endpoint hiccups even though the stored access token is still valid - converting a transient Salesforce outage into total Salesforce unavailability.
B: The constructor now performs a blocking remote POST to login.salesforce.com and a Prisma credential.update on every SalesforceCalendarService instantiation, where previously jsforce.Connection refreshed tokens lazily only when an access token expired. Every Salesforce calendar operation (and every booking touching Salesforce) now pays an extra OAuth round-trip plus a DB write per instantiation — a hot-path regression and a new network failure point that turns previously-cached-token operations into hard failures when Salesforce is slow or rate-limits.

Every booking operation touching a Salesforce calendar now incurs a synchronous round-trip to Salesforce and a DB write, burns Salesforce token-endpoint rate limits, and fails outright whenever Salesforce's token endpoint hiccups even though the stored access token is still valid - converting a transient Salesforce outage into total Salesforce unavailability.
B: The newly added Salesforce refresh block runs unconditionally inside connection setup — every time a jsforce.Connection is constructed the code fetches a fresh token from login.salesforce.com and writes it via prisma.credential.update, regardless of whether the existing access_token is expired. On any deployment with salesforce installed, each calendar operation that builds a service adds one outbound token request plus one credential DB write to the hot path, multiplying Salesforce API consumption and credential-row churn; token endpoint rate limits now gate ordinary calendar reads.
